newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks seen starting firmer but quiet.
newsitem.headline: French stocks seen starting firmer but quiet.

text.p: French shares were expected to rise at the opening on Tuesday, drawing support from firm bonds, the dollar and an overnight rise on Wall Street.

But traders said volumes have been low as the market stayed quiet ahead of U.S. indicators due this week and the May Day Thursday bank holiday, which usually becomes a four-day weekend as people take Friday off.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 13.99 points or 0.55 percent at 2,550.25 on Monday.
The CAC-40 futures contract on GLOBEX was up 10 at 2,565 at 0730 GMT from Monday's close.
"There's no business, volumes are very low," said a broker. "People are very hesitant," he added.

Investors are waiting on the result of the May 25-June 1 French parliamentary election, hoping for the return of a smaller but more disciplined centre-right majority which will support measures to allow France to meet its Maastricht commitments and adopt more liberal economic policies.
"Then the market will go through the roof," the broker said.
Markets also appeared to have priced in a potential rise in U.S. interest rates of up to 50 basis points in May, to dampen inflationary pressures, he added.
